expected.finding: **[P2]** [Field-only triggers never start topic mining](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py:694). The trigger string starts with a number (`"5 field failures..."`), but both mining conditions require `startswith("field")`. With healthy coverage and five recurring field failures, `decide()` returns no change even though `mine_topics()` produces a valid candidate. Use a boolean or structured trigger type.

**[P2]** [Successful shell output becomes false failure evidence](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/mine-trace-failures.py:177). Pattern matching counts successful `cat`/`rg` output containing error examples as actual failures. It also classifies `"10 passed, 0 failed"` as a test failure. This contaminates the anchor used to adjust policy weights and trigger rollbacks. Distinguish command failures from printed content and require positive failure counts.

**[P2]** [Deduplication discards commands needed for classification](/home/runner/work/open-inspect-72e95a/open-inspect-72e95a/scripts/mine-trace-failures.py:225). Failures are merged by `(tool, excerpt)`, although topic matching also uses the command. Two commands returning identical `Permission denied` messages retain only the first command. Reproducing this with synthetic `cat ordinary.txt` and `cat auth.json` events loses the authentication-topic evidence entirely. Include the command in the deduplication key or preserve all contributing commands.
